4) A chi possono essere comunicati i Suoi dati personali?
I Suoi dati personali potranno essere conosciuti dal personale della Società autorizzato al trattamento in ragione dello svolgimento delle proprie mansioni lavorative.
La Società, inoltre, potrà comunicare i Suoi dati personali a soggetti terzi che operano in qualità di Responsabili, appositamente nominati ai sensi dell'art. 28 del Regolamento, quali a titolo esemplificativo e non esaustivo società di gestione dei servizi e dei sistemi informatici.
Infine, i Suoi dati personali possono essere condivisi con autorità e/o enti che operano quali titolari autonomi del trattamento.
5) I Suoi dati personali possono essere trasferiti verso paesi al di fuori dello Spazio Economico Europeo?
Il trasferimento dei Suoi dati personali al di fuori dello Spazio Economico Europeo avverrà verso Paesi terzi per i quali la Commissione Europea abbia riconosciuto che essi garantiscono un livello di protezione adeguato ovvero in presenza di adeguate garanzie o delle specifiche deroghe previste dal Regolamento.
6) Per quanto tempo sono conservati i Suoi dati personali?
La Società conserva i dati in una forma che consente l'identificazione degli interessati per un arco di tempo necessario al conseguimento delle specifiche finalità per cui sono trattati, nel rispetto degli obblighi contrattuali e/o normativi. La durata dei singoli cookie è specificata nelle tabelle sopra riportate.
7) Quali sono i Suoi diritti?
La informiamo che Lei, in qualità di soggetto interessato al trattamento, può esercitare i seguenti diritti in merito al trattamento dei Suoi dati personali:
diritto di accesso: diritto di ottenere dal Titolare la conferma che sia o meno in corso un trattamento dei Suoi dati personali e in tal caso, di ottenere l'accesso agli stessi (fatto salvo che ciò non leda i diritti altrui);
diritto alla cancellazione ("oblio"): diritto di ottenere dal Titolare la cancellazione dei Suoi dati personali senza ingiustificato ritardo. La Società ha l'obbligo di procedere con la suddetta cancellazione qualora, a titolo meramente esemplificativo e non esaustivo:
i Suoi dati personali non siano più necessari rispetto alla finalità del trattamento;
i Suoi dati personali siano stati trattati illecitamente;
i Suoi dati personali debbano essere cancellati per adempiere ad un obbligo legale;
diritto alla limitazione del trattamento: diritto di ottenere dal Titolare la limitazione del trattamento. La Società ha l'obbligo di procedere con la suddetta limitazione qualora:
sia contestata l'esattezza dei Suoi dati personali (per il periodo necessario al Titolare per verificare l'esattezza di tali dati personali);
il trattamento sia illecito e Lei si sia opposto alla cancellazione dei Suoi dati personali e ne abbia richiesto la limitazione;

diritto alla portabilità dei dati: diritto di ricevere in un formato strutturato, di uso comune e leggibile da dispositivo automatico i Suoi dati personali e di trasmettere tali dati ad altro Titolare del trattamento, solo per i casi in cui il trattamento sia basato sul consenso o sul contratto e per i soli dati trattati tramite strumenti elettronici;
diritto di proporre un reclamo a un'Autorità di controllo: fatto salvo ogni altro ricorso amministrativo o giurisdizionale, qualora Lei ritenga che il trattamento che la riguarda violi il Regolamento, ha il diritto di proporre reclamo all'Autorità di Controllo dello Stato membro in cui risiede o lavora abitualmente, ovvero dello Stato in cui si è verificata la presunta violazione;

snapshots.text_content:
Chi siamo - Sefea Impact
Chi
siamo
I nostri principi
Centralità della persona
Mettiamo le persone e i loro bisogni al centro delle nostre scelte finanziarie, favorendo l’empowerment individuale e l’inclusione, con un’attenzione ai più vulnerabili.
Sostenibilità ambientale
I nostri investimenti puntano a ridurre l’impatto ambientale, promuovendo un futuro sostenibile e creando valore duraturo.
Cooperazione
Lavoriamo in sinergia con diversi attori del settore per ottenere risultati più efficaci e duraturi, rafforzando le reti di collaborazione.
Partecipazione
Coinvolgiamo
attivamente investitori, partner e stakeholder nei nostri processi, integrando il loro contributo per migliorare l’impatto finanziario e sociale.
Responsabilità
Valutiamo l’efficacia dei nostri investimenti misurando il cambiamento positivo che generano, garantendo un utilizzo responsabile delle risorse.
Trasparenza
Comunichiamo con chiarezza, condividendo azioni, risultati e obiettivi per garantire fiducia e comprensione.
Strategia di investimento
Gestiamo i nostri
prodotti finanziari adottando una strategia di
IMPACT INVESTING
.
Per noi,
l’IMPACT INVESTING
è una forma di investimento caratterizzata dall’
INTENZIONE
esplicita di affrontare problemi sociali e/o ambientali, oltre a generare un adeguato ritorno finanziario. Questo approccio richiede la
MISURAZIONE
e la gestione dell’impatto, e utilizza i dati per capire cosa funziona e cosa migliorare. Ci impegniamo affinché i nostri investimenti creino un
VALORE ADDIZIONALE
che non sarebbe stato possibile senza di essi.
INTENZIONALITÀ
MISURABILITÀ
ADDIZIONALITÀ
Engagement
nel settore
Ci impegniamo affinché la finanza a impatto cresca, favorendo la diffusione di modelli imprenditoriali e di investimento che mettono le persone, le relazioni e il pianeta al centro. Come?
Supportando lo sviluppo di
CONOSCENZE, COMPETENZE E STRUMENTI
nel settore.
Ricerca
Dottorato in collaborazione con Università di Bologna
Nel 2024 abbiamo
co-finanziato insieme all’Università di Bologna una
borsa di dottorato
all’interno del corso interdipartimentale in Public Governance, Management e Policy, con l’obiettivo di indagare quali modelli di impact investing sono generativi di valore sociale/ambientale.
SEFEA Impact
come case
s
tudy
SEFEA
Impact
è stata oggetto di
ricerca
come
caso studio
nei seguenti progetti:
ESG and impact litigation: identifying and governing the causes through strategic accountability patterns
Autori e autrici: Chiara Andreoli, Chiara Cremasco, Camilla Falivena, Sandro Brunelli
Finanza d’impatto sociale Istituzioni, capacity building e governance per l’innovazione
Autori e autrici: Giorgia Bonaga, Giulio Ecchia, Riccardo Prandini, Paolo Venturi
Università Federico II di Napoli, corso di laurea magistrale in economia aziendale. Tesi di laurea in governo ed etica d’impresa: Corporate Social Responsibility e Impact Investing: il Caso Sefea Impact SGR
Autrice: Daniela Axinte
ESCP Business School Social. Master Thesis: Enterprises and NGOs: Definitions, Funding Approaches and Measurement of Performance
Autore: Jacopo Jesse
Strumenti
Software IMM (Impact Measurement and Management) e scoring ESG
Abbiamo sviluppato in collaborazione con il centro di ricerca Tiresia del politecnico di Milano un
software proprietario per la misurazione e gestione dell’impatto e l’assessment ESG
delle società.
Questo strumento è utile per il monitoraggio e la tracciabilità delle performance dei nostri fondi e per i processi di IMM e sostenibilità delle nostre società partecipate.
Rappresentanza
Presidenza Forum per la Finanza Sostenibile
Massimo Giusti, Presidente e AD di SEFEA Impact, è
presidente
del
Forum per la Finanza Sostenibile
, associazione non profit nata nel 2001 con l’obiettivo di incoraggiare l’inclusione dei criteri ambientali, sociali e di governance (ESG) nei prodotti e nei processi finanziari.
Board SIA – Social Impact Agenda per l’Italia
Massimo Giusti, Presidente e AD di SEFEA Impact, è
membro del board
di
Social Impact Agenda per l’Italia
, associazione punto di riferimento della finanza a impatto in Italia. Social Impact Agenda per l’Italia è nata dall’evoluzione dell’Advisory Board italiano che nel 2013 si riunì nella Social Impact Investing Tasfkorce (SIIT), promossa nell’ambito del G8.
G
overnance
La nostra governance della SGR, unica nel panorama italiano, è
MULTISTAKEHOLDER
e riflette la sua mission:
è composta da una maggioranza di
ENTI NO PROFIT
(fondazioni, associazioni, imprese sociali, ecc.)
rispetta il
CRITERIO DELLA DIVERSIFICAZIONE
: nessun ente può singolarmente o insieme a un ente della stessa categoria detenere la maggioranza del capitale sociale
Rete
Collaboriamo con centri di ricerca ed esperti e partecipiamo a reti e associazioni della finanza
Il team
Consiglio di amministrazione
Massimo Giusti
Presidente e amministratore delegato
Massimo Giusti
, è un cooperatore sociale esperto di Terzo Settore, Finanza Sostenibile e Settore Immobiliare. Negli anni ha dato vita a varie cooperative sociali e consorzi e ha ricoperto posizioni apicali in enti del mondo cooperativo e del Terzo Settore. È attualmente Segretario Generale della Fondazione O.N.C. Organismo di controllo sui centri servizi del volontariato in Italia, Consigliere indipendente e non esecutivo per il Gruppo Hera spa, Presidente del Fondo Pensione “ARCO” e Consigliere del Fondo Pensione “PEGASO”. È decorato Pontificio oltre che dell’Ordine al Merito della Repubblica Italiana.
Giorgio Righetti
Consigliere e Vicepresidente
Giorgio Righetti
, è direttore generale di Acri dal primo settembre 2010 e vanta una esperienza combinata nel settore profit e non profit. Ha un’esperienza di oltre di oltre tre anni (2007-2010) alla direzione della Fondazione Con il Sud, della quale ha avviato la gestione operativa delle attività. È Consigliere di amministrazione di CDP Investimenti sgr dal 2015, e ricopre diversi incarichi di Consigliere di amministrazione in realtà non profit. È inoltre componente del Comitato di indirizzo strategico del Fondo per il contrasto della povertà educativa minorile (ex legge 208/2015) presso la Presidenza del Consiglio dei Ministri.
Eleonora Vanni
Consigliera
Eleonora Vanni
è Presidente di Legacoopsociali e Vicepresidente di Legacoop. Dal 2007 è impegnata nell’ambito della rappresentanza delle cooperative sociali. Già vicepresidente di Coopfond, è attualmente componente del CdA di Cooperazione Finanza Impresa.
È inoltre impegnata in organizzazioni del Terzo Settore ed è attualmente componente del Coordinamento del Forum Nazionale del Terzo Settore e dal 2018 è componente del Consiglio Nazionale del Terzo Settore.
Management Team
Sara D’Aulerio
Direzione operativa e Responsabile ESG e impatto
Sara D’Aulerio
si è laureata nel 2003 in Economia Politica all’Università di Bologna e ha poi conseguito un presso la stessa Università un Master in Studi di Genere e Politiche di Pari Opportunità e un Executive Master in Gestione della Sostenibilità Aziendale presso 24Ore Business School.
Entrata in SEFEA Holding S.C. nel 2007, dal 2013 segue la Direzione Operativa dell’intero Gruppo SEFEA fino al 2019. Nel 2016 partecipa alla costituzione di Sefea Impact SGR con il ruolo di Direttrice Operativa.
Maurizio Bertipaglia
Responsabile investimenti area Cooperazione e Impresa Sociale
Maurizio Bertipaglia
è laureato in Economia e Commercio. Ha un’esperienza ventennale nell’ambito della gestione amministrativa e della pianificazione economico finanziaria. È stato Responsabile amministrativo e Responsabile della pianificazione finanziaria per diverse istituzioni finanziarie, enti dedicati al sostegno delle PMI, enti operanti nel settore dell’economia sociale. Ha svolto numerosi incarichi in qualità di consulente, sindaco e amministratore di cooperative sociali operanti in Veneto.
Mauro Zan
Responsabile investimenti area Mercato
Mauro Zan
ha oltre 25 anni di esperienza in private equity, banking e corporate finance. Ha iniziato il suo percorso professionale nel gruppo Electrolux, ha lavorato poi presso UniCredit nell’ambito del team Nuova Europa. Nel 2011 viene nominato Responsabile del Dipartimento Investimenti presso FINEST. Attualmente è “Responsabile Investimenti a Mercato” di Sefea Impact S.g.r., siede inoltre nel CdA di alcune società partecipate.
Simone Gottardo
Responsabile amministrativo
Simone Gottardo
laureato in Economia e Commercio presso l’Università Ca ‘Foscari di Venezia e ha conseguito un Master in Banca & Finanza presso la Fondazione CUOA di Vicenza.  Ha iniziato la sua carriera nel 2000 presso la Direzione Bilancio e Partecipazioni della Banca Popolare di Vicenza, dal 2012 è stato referente amministrativo presso Akemia Sgr. Entra a far parte del team di Sefea Impact nel 2019 come responsabile amministrativo.
Elena Barison
Sustainabilty & Impact Analyst
Laureata in Management dell’Economia Sociale all’Università di Bologna, dal 2020 ha collaborato con il Dipartimento di Scienze Aziendali dell’Alma Mater come project manager sui temi dell’imprenditorialità sociale e dell’innovazione per la social economy. Dal 2023 ha lavorato in AICCON, occupandosi di direzione strategica, valutazione di impatto e reporting per organizzazioni e reti dell’economia sociale. In SEFEA Impact dal 2025, si occupa dello sviluppo del modello di impatto della SGR e dell’accompagnamento delle partecipate sui temi della sostenibilità e dell’impatto sociale.
Valentina Piccin
Analista finanziario
Valentina Piccin
si è laureata in Economia Aziendale, con specializzazione in Amministrazione e Controllo, presso l’Università di Udine nel 2016. Nel 2023 ha seguito il Corso Istituzionale AIFI. Ha lavorato come analista finanziario in un fondo d’investimento seguendo progetti di internazionalizzazione. Si è unita allo staff di SEFEA nel 2019 per valutare la dimensione economico-finanziaria degli investimenti proposti al Fondo.
Alessia Zanella
Finance & Accounting Specialist
Laureata in Economia e Commercio e in Economia e Gestione delle Aziende presso l’Univ

Fondi e progetti
Sinloc: oltre 15 anni di esperienza nella gestione di fondi e progetti.
Sinloc, consulenza e investimenti per lo sviluppo locale
Sinloc Investimenti SGR è parte del Gruppo SINLOC, realtà attiva in tutta Italia da circa 20 anni.
Il Gruppo ha come mission fondante la promozione dello sviluppo locale attraverso la realizzazione di infrastrutture strategiche, assistenza tecnica e un’attività d’investimento, che ha preso avvio nel 2008.
La capogruppo, Sinloc SpA, è partecipata da 12 tra le maggiori Fondazioni di Origine Bancaria, e opera al fianco di istituzioni pubbliche, imprese ed enti del Terzo Settore nella configurazione e realizzazione dei loro progetti, anche attraverso l’accesso a risorse finanziarie nazionali ed europee.
Il Gruppo Sinloc riunisce, oltre alla capogruppo, società strumentali partecipate, focalizzate su specifici comparti di mercato e società di progetto che realizzano e gestiscono iniziative, soprattutto in Partenariato Pubblico Privato.

Our Team
About Us
It is an initiative founded on the concept of “family” as the basis for sustainable business and creativity, which supports visionary entrepreneurs by letting them do their job well, as they have done for decades. It is an evergreen investment holding specialized in minority, private equity and private investments in public equity (so called “PIPE”) transactions. It has an exclusive focus on excellent Italian small and medium-sized companies, listed, unlisted or in the pre-IPO phase. It is characterized, also in the investment approach, by an entrepreneurial and long-term DNA. It represents a diversified bouquet of italian excellent companies
Smart Capital’s Team
Andrea Costantini
Chairman and CEO, Managing Partner
Andrea graduated at Bocconi University in Business Economics and Legislation and holds an executive MBA at Harvard Business School.
Executive Vice President at Agrati Group. 12 years abroad (Singapore and USA) as manager for The Coca-Cola Company and d’Amico Shipping. Experience also in KPMG and Arthur Andersen. Confindustria Board Member. Past Member in Bocconi Alumni Community’s Counsel of Administration and Harvard Board Member.
Andrea Faraggiana
General Manager and Managing Partner
Andrea Faraggiana, graduated at Bocconi University with Bachelor Degree and Master of Science in Finance.​
Deputy General Manager, Investment Director and Investment Committee Member in several primary listed investment companies (First Capital and T.I.P.) with experience in Investment Banking and M&A between Milan and London (Lazard and Rothschild).​ Board Member in several listed and unlisted companies.
Roberto Francani
Advisory and Business Development Director, Partner
Roberto Francani, graduated in Economics and Banking at Milano Bicocca University and MSc In Management, Finance and International Business at Bergamo University with foreign qualifications at London School of Economics, Tippie College of Business – Iowa University and Goldman Sachs.
He has worked in several sectors, encompassing Investment banking, M&A, family offices and Private Equity, coordinating people, originating and managing different deals across industries at European level. He was Board Member in several unlisted companies.
Dino Catena
Value Creation Director
Dino graduated at Bocconi University in Business Economics (major in Finance).
Business executive with a commercial imprinting and a solid financial background. Consolidated experience in several industries (Food, Durable Goods, Banking – capital markets).
Michele Vabanesi
Investment Associate
Michele Vabanesi earned a Bachelor’s degree in Economics and Business Management from Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore in Milan in 2018 and a Master’s degree in Administration, Finance and Control from Bocconi University in Milan in 2021.
He gained solid experience by holding the position of Investment Analyst Intern at Europa Investimenti in Milan in 2020 and the position of Credit Underwriter Intern at Credimi in Milan in 2019. He has been on the board of AIFI Young as an advisor since 2023.
Ippolito Fiori
CFO Services and Business Development
Ippolito Fiori graduated at Bocconi University with an MSc in Accounting, Financial Management and Control.
He gained solid professional experience first at Arthur Andersen and then, with over 20 years abroad, at the Ferrero Group where he held various positions, including Area CFO and Group Chief Administrative Officer.
Matteo Conti
Investment Analyst
Matteo Conti earned a Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Production Engineering from the Lecco territorial pole of the Politecnico of Milan in 2019 and a Master’s degree in the Finance branch of Management Engineering from the Politecnico of Milan in 2022.
In 2023 he has been a member of Organizing Committee for the Associazione Italiana di Ingegneria Gestionale’s XXXIV Annual Scientific Meeting in Lecco. In 2022, he has been a Researcher at the Entrepreneurship Finance & Innovation Observatories of the Politecnico di Milano, assuming the role of Project Manager of the Crowdinvesting Observatory and University Assistant in the course of Economics and Business Organization for the Bachelor degree in Automation Engineering since 2023.
Laura Pedrinazzi
Technology Director
Laura Pedrinazzi, graduated in Computer Science and Bioengineering, PhD in Bioengineering and Bioinformatics at University of Pavia and Master in Business Strategy and Business Transformation at Sole24Ore Business School. ​
Laura has a strong background in software development, artificial intelligence and smart cities. She joined to various international R&D projects in academic environment and collaborating, along her professional career, with different and heterogeneous technological company.​

January 27, 2026
Stirling Square-backed Sustainable Agro Solutions expands product portfolio and capabilities in microorganisms through the acquisition of Ceres Biotics
Lleida and Madrid, Spain, 27 January 2026:
Stirling Square Capital Partners (“Stirling Square”), a leading pan-European mid-market private equity firm, today announces that its portfolio company Sustainable Agro Solutions (“SAS Group”), a leading developer and producer of biostimulants, soil conditioners, defence activators and other specialty plant nutrition solutions for the agricultural sector, has acquired Ceres Biotics, a biotechnology company specialised in sustainable biosolutions based on microorganisms. Financial terms of the transaction have not been disclosed.
The acquisition of Ceres Biotics marks another significant milestone in SAS Group’s strategy to build a global leader in agricultural biosolutions. Ceres Biotics brings a highly complementary product portfolio, a robust presence in Europe, trusted and top-quality customer relationships, and strong R&D capabilities focused on obtaining and developing highly efficient probiotic strains. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Spain, Ceres has established itself as an innovator, with more than 550 proprietary strains, robust R&D capabilities, and a strong international profile, trading across more than 20 countries in Europe and beyond.
Stirling Square acquired a majority stake in SAS in July 2021 and has since supported the company’s growth through both organic initiatives – including investments in R&D, product development, development of a new production plant, and market expansion, among others – and targeted acquisitions. Under Stirling Square’s ownership, SAS has significantly accelerated its international growth strategy and strengthened its position as a leader in sustainable agricultural solutions.
Eduard Vallverdú, Chief Executive Officer of SAS Group, commented:
“This is an incredibly exciting moment for SAS Group as we undertake an acquisition that marks our expansion into the large and growing field of microbial biosolutions. The talented Ceres Biotics team possesses deep expertise in the microorganisms space and has built an impressive business with significant growth potential. With a high-quality and complementary product portfolio, and its best-in-class R&D capabilities, Ceres Biotics is uniquely positioned for future success. Ceres Biotics’ pioneering work and impressive R&D capabilities in the microorganisms field are highly complementary to our strategy. Together, we will offer a broader, more innovative portfolio to our customers, supporting the transition to more sustainable and productive agriculture. By combining our joint capabilities, we will unlock significant opportunities to reinforce our value proposition, scale production, and broaden customer reach, both in Europe and abroad. We welcome the Ceres Biotics team to SAS Group and look forward to driving continued expansion and long-term value creation together.”
Emilio Marín and Mónica Perdices, Co-Founders of Ceres Biotics, stated:
“We are proud of how far Ceres Biotics has come and grateful to our team and partners who have supported us throughout the last 15 years. As part of this next chapter at the heart of SAS Group, we believe Ceres Biotics is uniquely positioned to reach new heights, enhance value for our customers, and offer new opportunities to our employees. This is a crucial step in our journey, and we are delighted that Ceres Biotics is joining SAS Group, which shares our heritage and vision, both underpinned by a strong commitment to R&D and innovation. We see this partnership as a recognition of the quality and dedication of the Ceres Biotics team, and we are excited to see the company continue its growth as part of SAS Group.”
Enrico Biale, Partner at Stirling Square Capital Partners, added:
“We are thrilled to announce the combination of SAS and Ceres Biotics, which further demonstrates our commitment to supporting SAS Group’s growth, both organically and inorganically. Ceres Biotics brings deep expertise in the microorganisms space, a robust presence in Europe, and strong customer relationships. The highly complementary nature of Ceres Biotics’ business - geographically, from a product perspective, and technologically - makes this a highly strategic acquisition for SAS. This is another significant step forward in our ambition to create one of the global leading players in the biosolutions sector.”
Deloitte (due diligence) and Cuatrecasas advised SAS and Stirling Square. Ceres Biotics was advised by KPMG (corporate finance).
About Stirling Square Capital Partners
Stirling Square Capital Partners was founded in 2002 as a pan-European private equity firm specialised in internationalising and digitalising mid-market businesses with an enterprise value between EUR 100m and EUR 500m. The firm manages EUR 3.5bn on behalf of a global and diverse investor base. Since inception, Stirling Square has invested in 30+ platform companies and 100+ add-on acquisitions globally, helping to create regional and global champions. For more information, visit
www.stirlingsquare.com
.
About SAS Group
SAS is a group of companies whose objective is to lead the international market of biosolutions and plant nutrition products for the agricultural sector. Headquartered in Lleida (Spain), SAS is a global company present in more than 100 countries and with subsidiaries in different markets of interest. Its NOBA technology platform is a reference in the research of new solutions for agriculture. SAS Group is fully committed to sustainability, placing it at the heart of its business model.
About Ceres Biotics
Founded in 2010, Ceres Biotics is a Spanish company focused on sustainable solutions for agriculture, particularly in the segment of microbial biofertilizers and biostimulants. Ceres has built a reputation for quality, innovation, and customer service, serving clients in over 20 countries, including some of the world’s largest crop protection, fertilizers, and biostimulants companies.

Stirling Square Capital Partners announces the sale of Isoclima Group to Fondo Italiano di Investimento and The Equity Club
Close
December 29, 2025
Stirling Square Capital Partners announces the sale of Isoclima Group to Fondo Italiano di Investimento and The Equity Club
London and Este (Padua), 23 December 2025
– Stirling Square Capital Partners (“Stirling Square”), a leading pan-European mid-market private equity firm, announces the sale of Isoclima Group (“Isoclima” or the “Company”), the global leader in innovative transparent solutions, to a consortium of financial investors led by Fondo Italiano d’Investimento SGR (”FII”), a leading platform for Italian private capital with a multi-strategy approach, and TEC Glass, an independent vehicle established by the investors participating in the club deal initiative sponsored by The Equity Club (“TEC”). Financial terms of the transaction, which is subject to customary closing conditions, have not been disclosed.
Founded in Italy in 1977, Isoclima has grown into a world-class provider of glass and composite materials solutions that enhance personal safety, security and sustainability across a variety of sectors including aerospace, armoured and high-performance vehicles, yachting, and security architecture. The Company is recognised as the partner of choice for a wide spread of demanding clients based on its advanced design and development capabilities, extensive patent portfolio, and commitment to impeccable service.
Under Stirling Square’s stewardship, Isoclima transitioned from family leadership to a professional management team embodying institutional and entrepreneurial qualities. The Company expanded operations across Italy and Croatia while refocusing on priority growth areas such as aerospace, military and architectural security applications. Isoclima further internationalised its business with the acquisition of two specialty glass makers in the United States and a strategic partnership in Colombia, which earned it full exposure to the fast-growing markets in the Americas. With Stirling Square’s support, Isoclima also progressed its digital and sustainability transformation; new capabilities were introduced to boost operating efficiency and elevate customer experience, enhancing the Company’s competitive positioning and operating margins.
Gregorio Napoleone, Founder and Executive Chairman, at Stirling Square Capital Partners, commented:
“We are proud to have supported Isoclima’s multi-pronged transformation throughout our ownership. Our partnership with the original founder and a newly appointed management team has led the Company to new strategic and performance heights, as evidenced by the doubling of revenues and profits. This transaction builds on Stirling Square’s track record of partnering with family businesses and delivering ambitious, transformational value creation. We are excited for the continuing growth prospects of the business, and wish the talented team led by Liviana Forza all the best as they embark on a new chapter in their storied history.”
Liviana Forza, CEO of Isoclima Group, commented:
“Stirling Square’s support has enabled Isoclima to evolve into the global benchmark for advanced transparent solutions. By investing in our people, operational footprint, proprietary IP and distinctive capabilities, we have built a strong foundation for long-term growth and excellence. I am thrilled to welcome FII and TEC as shareholders and look forward to working with them towards our future expansion plans.”

STYLE CAPITAL - TEAM
overview
valori
team
perché scegliere noi
Roberta Benaglia
Amministratore Delegato
Profilo
Roberta Benaglia, laureata con lode in Ingegneria Gestionale presso il Politecnico di Milano, ha iniziato la sua esperienza professionale nel Listing Department di Borsa Italiana. Successivamente ha maturato un'esperienza ventennale nel Private Equity: la prima esperienza nel PE risale al 2001, con la collaborazione in Onetone Consulting, società di advisory del Fondo di Venture Capital Onetone, dedicato ad investimenti in società di ICT/Media ad alto potenziale di sviluppo. Dal 2003 ha lavorato per DGPA&Co – Area Advisory del Fondo di Private Equity Absolute Ventures SCA.
Dal 2005 è Socio Fondatore di STYLE CAPITAL SGR (già DGPA SGR). Durante questi anni Roberta ha contribuito al lancio (nel 2007) e alla gestione del fondo DGPA Capital, quale responsabile degli investimenti del Fondo in ambito "Fashion & Luxury" (oltre il 50% del capitale investito del Fondo). In particolare, Roberta ha seguito le operazioni Twinset, Sundek, Damiani, sedendo nei Consigli di Amministrazione anche con ruoli esecutivi, e Golden Goose con il ruolo di CEO e Chairman.
Dal 2016, Roberta è CEO e principale azionista della rinnovata SGR che promuove il secondo Fondo, STYLE CAPITAL.
Ad oggi Roberta ricopre il ruolo di Presidente del CdA di ZIMMERMANN, Executive Chairman di MSGM e Presidente di forte_forte, Vice Presidente esecutivo di LuisaViaRoma e Presidente del CdA di SOEUR.
Massimiliano Caraffa
Managing Partner & Chief Investment Officer
Profilo
Massimiliano Caraffa è entrato in Style Capital nel gennaio 2026 in qualità di Managing Partner e Chief Investment Officer.
Prima di entrare in Style Capital, Massimiliano ha trascorso oltre 20 anni in Carlyle, dove è stato Partner e Head of Consumer per l'Europa. In questo periodo ha partecipato a oltre 20 operazioni a livello globale e ha investito direttamente €2,4 miliardi di equity per Carlyle Europe. Nel corso degli anni ha ricoperto il ruolo di membro del board o Presidente in 15 società in portafoglio, nonché di membro del board di AIFI, l'Associazione Italiana del Private Equity, lavorando a stretto contatto con imprenditori e management team su progetti di espansione internazionale, sviluppo del brand, crescita operativa e creazione di valore nel lungo periodo. Tra le operazioni più rilevanti figurano Moncler, Golden Goose, Supreme e Flos B&B Italia Group.
Il suo lavoro è stato riconosciuto con numerosi premi di settore per operazioni di rilievo nei settori Fashion e Luxury, tra cui due riconoscimenti EVCA come 'European Private Equity Deal of the Year'. È inoltre co-autore di case study MBA e lecturer presso primarie business school internazionali, tra cui INSEAD e IESE.
All'inizio della sua carriera ha lavorato come consulente in McKinsey & Company. È laureato in Ingegneria Elettronica, magna cum laude, presso l'Università di Genova e ha conseguito un MBA presso INSEAD. È fluente in italiano, inglese e spagnolo.
Francesca Grosso
Director
Profilo
Francesca Grosso, in STYLE CAPITAL SGR (già DGPA SGR) dal 2008, si è laureata con lode all'Università Bocconi di Milano e ha iniziato la sua carriera nella Divisione Corporate Finance di E. Capital Partners ricoprendo ruoli di origination e execution di mandati M&A e finanza strutturata.
Nel 2008 Francesca ha conseguito l'abilitazione alla professione di Dottore Commercialista e Revisore Contabile.
Successivamente si è occupata di Private Equity dal 2008 prima in DGPA SGR  e in seguito (dal 2016) nella rinnovata SGR STYLE CAPITAL. In particolare, Francesca ha seguito le operazioni Twin-Set, Damiani, Golden Goose, forte_forte e MSGM ed è attualmente Board Member di MSGM, forte_forte e Soeur.
Filippo Prini
Director
Profilo
Filippo Prini ha conseguito un MBA presso la Columbia Business School (NY) e una laurea in Business Administration & Finance presso la Fordham University (NY). È entrato a far parte di Style Capital nel settembre 2022 per dedicarsi al nuovo fondo Style Capital II. In precedenza Filippo ha trascorso 9 anni in Consulenza Strategica presso The Boston Consulting Group (BCG) trascorrendo 4 anni a Milano, 2 a NY e 3 a Parigi.
Durante la sua esperienza in BCG, è arrivato a prender parte della leadership team sia della practice Fashion & Luxury che della practice Principal Investors & Private Equity.
Durante il suo ultimo ruolo in BCG come Sr. Project Leader, ha guidato numerosi team sui seguenti ambiti: costruzioni di Business Plan, rafforzamento dei canali Digital & Omnicanali, Business Due Diligence sia Sell che Buy side, Turnarounds aziendali, e espansione ed ottimizzazione della rete retail.
Filippo parla fluentemente inglese, francese, tedesco e italiano.
Matteo Nulli
Director
Profilo
Matteo Nulli entra a far parte del team di investimento di STYLE CAPITAL nel 2019.
Ha maturato conoscenza del settore del lusso come analista presso Intesa Sanpaolo Corporate and Investment Banking ricoprendo ruoli di origination e execution di mandati M&A e finanza strutturata nella divisione Retail & Luxury dell'Istituto. Precedentemente Matteo è stato Senior Associate per PwC Deals Advisory nel team Transaction Services.
Ha conseguito un master in Finanza presso ESADE Business School (Barcellona), laureato con lode presso l'Università di Brescia in Economia e Gestione Aziendale, ha partecipato ad un anno di scambio all'estero presso la Nottingham Trent University.
Matteo ricopre attualmente il ruolo di CEO in Oceania (Holdco del Gruppo Zimmermann) e in precedenza ha ricoperto il ruolo di membro del CdA del Gruppo Zimmermann.
Federica Murgolo
Investment Manager
Profilo
Federica Murgolo è entrata in Style Capital a Dicembre 2022 per dedicarsi al nuovo fondo Style Capital II.
Ha maturato competenze in ambito M&A durante i 4 anni trascorsi nel Transaction Services di PwC Deals Advisory, dove ha fornito servizi di Due Diligence finanziaria, sell e buy side, lavorando a stretto contatto con fondi di private equity e grandi aziende. Federica ha partecipato a diversi progetti nei settori fashion, retail & consumer, industrial manufacturing, TMT e pharma & healthcare.
Federica ha una laurea specialistica in Finanza presso l'Alma Mater Studiorum - Università di Bologna e una laurea triennale in Economia aziendale. Nel 2018 ha partecipato ad un master con focus sul processo di M&A presso la Bayes Business School di Londra.
Diego Francesco Tonelli
Associate
Profilo
Diego Tonelli è entrato in STYLE CAPITAL nel giugno 2024 per occuparsi dei nuovi investimenti di Style Capital II e del monitoraggio delle performance delle società attualmente in portafoglio.
Ha maturato esperienza in M&A e strategia aziendale nel ruolo di Associate Consultant presso Bain & Company, dove è stato membro della practice Fashion & Luxury.
Nel corso della sua esperienza in Bain, Diego ha lavorato su diversi progetti per brand del fashion & luxury e per investitori finanziari, su temi quali la definizione di Business Plan, Retail Excellence, Strategia Digitale & Omnicanale, Ottimizzazione dei Costi IT, oltre a Commercial Due Diligence sell-side e buy-side.
Ha conseguito un Master in Corporate Finance presso la Fordham University e una Laurea in Filosofia, Politica ed Economia presso il King's College di Londra.
Alessia Ruggi
Analyst
Profilo
Alessia Ruggi è entrata in Style Capital nel gennaio 2026, dove si occupa delle attività di investimento del fondo Style Capital II e del monitoraggio delle performance delle società in portafoglio.
In precedenza ha maturato esperienza in consulenza strategica presso OC&C Strategy Consultants e Boston Consulting Group, lavorando a stretto contatto con sponsor di Private Equity su progetti di commercial due diligence, pianificazione strategica e value creation, con focus sui settori consumer, fashion & luxury e services.
Alessia ha conseguito una Laurea Magistrale in Management presso l'Università Commerciale Luigi Bocconi e una Laurea Triennale in Economia e Amministrazione delle Imprese presso la stessa università.
Lorenzo Marini
Analyst
Profilo
Lorenzo Marini entra a far parte del team di investimento di STYLE CAPITAL nel gennaio 2026.
Dal 2022 ha maturato esperienza in Corporate Finance in PwC Deals Advisory come Senior Associate e membro di Edge - PwC Deals Graduate Programme for EMEA. Nei Team di M&A e Strategy & Teams, Lorenzo ha sviluppato competenze trasversali in ambito M&A.
Lorenzo ha conseguito una laurea specialistica in Finanza presso l'Università Ca' Foscari di Venezia.
Laura Savarino
CFO
Profilo
Laura Savarino si è laureata in Economia Aziendale presso l'Università di Castellanza (LIUC) nel 2003. Laura ha iniziato la sua carriera all'AIFI (Associazione Italiana del Private Equity e Venture Capital) lavorando dal 2003 al 2006 nel Tax & Legal department.
Nel 2007 Laura entra a far parte di Principia SGR, una società di gestione di fondi chiusi di venture capital, dove gestisce problematiche di carattere legale, amministrativo e contabile, oltre agli affari societari; dal 2009 al 2015 ricopre il ruolo di Responsabile dell'area amministrazione/operations della società. Laura si è poi spostata in Opera SGR in cui è stata responsabile dell'area Amministrazione, Finanza e Controllo. Dal 2016 è entrata a far parte del Team di STYLE CAPITAL come responsabile amministrativo e organizzativo (CFO) e componente del Consiglio di Amministrazione.
È anche Presidente di Oceania (Holdco del Gruppo Zimmermann) e Consigliere di Amministrazione di Florence Srl (Holdco del Gruppo LUISAVIAROMA).

COME INVESTIAMO
ESIGENZE DELL'IMPRESA TARGET
Investimenti: beni materiali (impianti, macchinari, attrezzature, ecc.), beni immateriali (ricerche di mercato, brevetti, campagne pubblicitarie, ecc.), processo produttivo (sviluppo di nuovi prodotti, commesse pluriennali, ecc.).
Penetrazione dei mercati internazionali.
Crescita per linee esterne: acquisizione di altre imprese, aggregazioni / integrazioni di filiera.
Gestione del passaggio generazionale e/o cambiamenti nella compagine sociale.
CARATTERISTICHE TIPICHE DELL'OPERAZIONE
Operazioni di Capitale di Minoranza
tramite sottoscrizione di aumenti di capitale. Possibilità di acquisto di partecipazioni nell’ambito di processi di riorganizzazione della base sociale.
Operazioni di Finanziamento
attraverso strumenti estremamente flessibili e modulabili in relazione alle specifiche esigenze dei piani di sviluppo aziendali. Normalmente, gli strumenti di private debt abbinano ad una remunerazione cedolare contenuta un meccanismo di compartecipazione alla crescita di valore dell’impresa.
Taglio dell’Investimento
: da un minimo di 500 mila euro ad un massimo di 5 milioni di euro.
Durata dell’Investimento
: compresa tra i 3 e i 7 anni.
VANTAGGI PER L'IMPRESA TARGET
Patrimonializzazione: attraverso l’intervento di SICI è possibile definire una politica di finanziamento del Piano Industriale solida e coerente con gli obiettivi di crescita, riequilibrando la composizione delle fonti di finanziamento utilizzate.
Permette all’imprenditore di mantenere il controllo decisionale e di disporre di un supporto qualificato in ogni decisione strategica, nella gestione dei processi non routinari e nelle operazioni straordinarie.
Rappresenta un elemento riconosciuto e apprezzato dal mercato e dagli interlocutori chiave dell’impresa, consentendo miglioramenti nel rating bancario (con benefici in termini economici e di ulteriore credito) e l’accesso a qualificate competenze finanziarie potendo far leva sulla vasta rete di rapporti professionali ed istituzionali che SICI mette a disposizione per il raggiungimento degli obiettivi di sviluppo.
TEMPI E PROCESSO DELL'INVESTIMENTO
Pre-Analisi
: l’opportunità di investimento è valutata in prima battuta dal Team di SICI che ne valuta la coerenza con le politiche di investimento.
Pre-Negoziazione
: la struttura e le linee guida dell’operazione sono condivise con l’Imprenditore (determinazione del valore di impresa, future regole di governance e modalità di uscita a termine). Le parti possono eventualmente sottoscrivere una Lettera di Intenti non vincolante (LOI).
Istruttoria del Soggetto Garante:
Sulla base delle caratteristiche dell’operazione e della rischiosità dello strumento finanziario, la SGR può richiedere il rilascio di garanzie, anche presso finanziarie specializzate.
Istruttoria dell’Investimento
: analisi approfondita dell’opportunità di investimento e del programma di  sviluppo dell’impresa. Redazione dell’Information Memorandum e presentazione del dossier al Risk Manager (per la redazione di una relazione che illustra i principali rischi operativi, finanziari e di credito dell’impresa target) e al Comitato Tecnico del Fondo (“CT”) che formula un parere obbligatorio sulla convenienza/opportunità di perfezionare l’intervento. Presentazione del dossier anche al Comitato di Vigilanza sui Conflitti di Interesse (“CVCI”). Nel caso di fondi di venture capital può essere istituito un Comitato Scientifico chiamato a formulare un parere obbligatorio ma non vincolante.
Delibera del CDA
: il C.d.A. di SICI esamina l’Information Memorandum, acquisisce il parere del CT e del CVCI e delibera sull’opportunità di procedere all’investimento, ordinando, ove ritenute necessarie e/o opportune le attività Due Diligence.
Definizione del Contratto di Investimento
: il Team di SICI e l’Imprenditore, con l’eventuale supporto dei consulenti incaricati, definiscono il Contratto di Investimento, i Patti parasociali e ogni altro accordo eventualmente correlato.
Signing e Closing
: si procede con la firma dei contratti e l’esecuzione dell’operazione attraverso l’erogazione delle risorse.
Tempi di analisi e finalizzazione dell’operazione
: mediamente 4-8 mesi.

CHI SIAMO
STORY LINE
1998
– Sviluppo Imprese Centro Italia S.p.A. nasce a Firenze per iniziativa di Fidi Toscana, MPS Capital Services, CR Firenze e CR Lucca-Pisa-Livorno quale strumento sperimentale e congiunto per agire nell’ambito del Private Equity, allora nuovo segmento del mercato finanziario con forti potenzialità di sviluppo.
1999
– SICI lancia il primo Fondo di Investimento mobiliare chiuso “
CENTROINVEST
” con una dotazione iniziale di 38 milioni di Euro, destinato agli interventi in PMI del Centro Italia.
2003
– Completati gli investimenti con il CENTROINVEST, i Soci fondatori della SGR decidono di aprire il capitale sociale di SICI ad altre Banche e di rendere stabile la struttura manageriale e l’operatività della Società nell’ottica di renderla una SGR indipendente ed autonoma nel panorama finanziario toscano.
2004
– SICI lancia il secondo Fondo di Investimento mobiliare Chiuso “
FONDO TOSCANA VENTURE
” con una dotazione iniziale di 50 milioni di Euro, destinato agli interventi in PMI del Centro Italia e specificatamente della Toscana, riservando il 15% delle risorse totali ad interventi in start up innovative e tecnologiche.
2008
– Forte dell’esperienza e della conoscenza sviluppate nel settore e sul territorio, SICI lancia il suo terzo Fondo d’Investimento, il “
FONDO TOSCANA INNOVAZIONE
” (24,8 milioni di Euro), il primo specificatamente dedicato al comparto del Venture Capital e destinato a sostenere PMI innovative toscane, anche nelle primissime fasi di vita.
2012
– SICI inizia la raccolta per il quarto Fondo di Investimento: il “
FONDO RILANCIO E SVILUPPO
” inizia la sua operatività con dotazione di 26 milioni di Euro, “capitale per la crescita” destinato a PMI del Centro Italia che nel medio termine possano diventare un “nucleo di campioni” capaci di sostenere le sfide della competitività internazionale.
2014
– Gepafin S.p.A., società finanziaria partecipata dalla Regione Umbria e da 11 istituti di credito del territorio, entra nel capitale sociale di SICI SGR rilevando una quota del 14%.
2020
– SICI, con le risorse messe a disposizione dalla Regione Umbria nell’ambito del POR FESR 2014-2020, lancia il “
FONDO UMBRIA RICERCA E INNOVAZIONE
”, con una dotazione di 6,5 milioni di Euro destinato ad iniziative ad alto contenuto innovativo promosse da start up, PMI, e Grandi imprese attive nel territorio umbro.
2023
– Liquidazione del “
FONDO TOSCANA INNOVAZIONE
“.
2024
– SICI, con le risorse messe a disposizione dalla Regione Toscana, lancia il “
FONDO SVILUPPO COOPERAZIONE TOSCANA
” indirizzato a imprese cooperative regolarmente iscritte all’Albo e ubicate nel territorio toscano.

Experienced deal professionals, investing together as a core team since 2008. Dedicated in-house Value Creation and Sustainability experts.
At Three Hills, we have a diverse team united by common principles: entrepreneurial spirit, intellectual honesty, enthusiasm and an unwavering commitment to do better.
Investment Professionals
Mauro Moretti
Founder & CEO
Mauro is the Founder and CEO of Three Hills, of which he chairs the Investment Advisory Commitee of both Three Hills Capital Solutions and Impact strategies. Prior to establishing the company Mauro was a Partner at Hutton Collins where he worked on several investments. Earlier in his career he worked at BC Partners, both in Milan and London and the M&A division of J.P. Morgan.
Mauro is also the Founder and Chairman of the Nice To Meet You Foundation, a not-for-profit organisation, focused on promoting education through scholarships, research and projects, to guarantee the same opportunities for everyone and enhance their possibilities for change.
Mauro graduated cum laude in Business Administration from Bocconi University and completed his Master in Finance at Copenhagen Business School. He speaks Italian and English.
Marco Anatriello
Partner
Marco joined Three Hills as a Partner in January 2021 and is an Investment Advisory Committee Member of both the Capital Solutions and Impact strategies. Prior to joining the Firm, Marco was a Co-founder, Partner and Member of the Board of Bluegem Capital Partners, a successful Pan-European consumer focused fund which raised since inception and during his tenure more than €800m of capital across three primary funds and a secondary platform. At Bluegem Marco worked on several investments across Europe and sat on several companies’ Boards. Earlier in his career he worked at Merrill Lynch in the Investment Banking team and in the Strategic Solutions Group both in Milan and London, gaining exposure to M&A, equity and debt-linked products and fixed-income derivatives.
Marco is a member of Consiglio Direttivo of AIFI, and he regularly features in panels and conferences organised, among others, by AIFI, PE Insight and BVCA.
Marco graduated summa cum laude in Business Administration at Bocconi University after spending one academic semester at the University of Southern California – Marshall School of Business in Los Angeles. He speaks Italian, English and some Spanish.
Pablo Vélez
Partner
Pablo joined Three Hills as a Partner in April 2022 and is an Investment Advisory Committee Member of both the Capital Solutions and Impact strategies. Prior to joining the firm, Pablo was a Managing Director within the European Principal Group at Oaktree Capital Management where he lead deals in which over €1 billion of LP funds were invested from both the private equity funds and the direct lending funds. Earlier in his career, he worked in the Lehman Brothers Merchant Banking Group and its successor fund investing in Europe. Before that, he was based in New York and invested in Latin America while at DB Capital Partners, the private equity arm of Deutsche Bank.
Pablo is an Industrial Engineer from Universidad de los Andes in Colombia and holds an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School. He is fluent in Spanish.
Pauline Ammeux
Partner
Pauline joined Three Hills in 2024 as a Partner, responsible for our investing activities in France across all strategies, Prior to joining Three Hills, she served in top-ranked pan-European private equity firms (PAI Partners, BlackFin CP and Adagia) with a focus on the French middle market. She primarily focused on investments in the B2B services, financial services, and light industrials sectors. As a Board Member of numerous portfolio companies throughout her career, she has supported a diverse array of management teams with their international expansion, buy-and-build programmes, and ESG transformation processes. She started her career in 2007 in investment banking at Lazard in Paris, with extensive M&A experience through a subsequent tenure at Merrill Lynch as well.
Pauline graduated in business administration from HEC Paris and from Sciences Po (Paris Institute of Political Studies). She speaks French, English, and Intermediate German.
Abhik Das
Partner
Abhik joined Three Hills as a Partner in September 2022 with the objective to open Three Hills’ New York office. Prior to that, Abhik was a Managing Director and the Head of Private Debt at Golding Capital Partners, a European asset manager specialized in private markets investments. Abhik oversaw the successful growth of Golding’s private credit business and was responsible for all new fund and co-investments, as well as the management of the portfolio across Europe and North America. Prior to joining Golding, Abhik was a Partner in the Private Debt Group of BlueBay Asset Management in London (now Arcmont Asset Management), where he successfully invested close to €1bn in various middle market businesses across Europe. Before that, he worked in the Principal Finance team at Macquarie, where he invested across the capital structure of European and North American companies. He started his career in investment banking at Lehman Brothers in London.
Abhik graduated from the University of St. Gallen, Switzerland with an M.A. in Law and Economics (with honors). He also holds a dual CEMS MIM Master’s in International Management degree from ESADE Barcelona and the University of St. Gallen. He speaks English, German / Swiss German, French, Italian and Spanish.
Lance Contento
Partner
Lance joined Three Hills in January 2016 and is a Partner of the firm. He contributed to Three Hills’ New York office opening and activity, and is currently based in the United States. Before joining the company, Lance was in the Special Situations Group at Goldman Sachs where he focused on special situations lending in the U.S. middle market. Prior to that Lance held investment banking roles at Cogent Partners and Bank of America Securities.
Lance holds a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago, as well as an MBA and Masters in Advanced Finance from IE Business School in Madrid. He is a CFA Charterholder and speaks English and Spanish.
Arjan Blok
Managing Director
Arjan joined Three Hills in June 2017 and is a Managing Director and an Investment Advisory Committee Member of Three Hills’ Impact strategy. He is focused on the Benelux region and, since 2023, on TH Impact. Before joining the company, Arjan was at Vitruvian Partners where he worked for 2 years in the Benelux and UK investment teams. Prior to Vitruvian, he spent nearly 3 years in the Investment Banking division of Morgan Stanley covering Benelux and Switzerland. Previously, Arjan was a technology entrepreneur, co-founding an e-commerce software enterprise in the Netherlands.
Arjan holds a BSc in Business Administration and an MSc in Finance and Investments from the RSM Erasmus University in Rotterdam. He also holds a LL.M. in Financial Law from the ESL Erasmus University. Arjan speaks English and Dutch.
Barbara Roversi
Managing Director
Barbara joined Three Hills in March 2019 and is a Managing Director and an Investment Advisory Committee Member of Three Hills’ Impact strategy, as well as CEO of the Nice to Meet You foundation. Before joining the company, she worked for Metric Capital Partners in London, where she focused on new investment opportunities in SME’s across Europe. Prior to that, she was at Alvarez and Marsal where she served in their Financial Restructuring and Performance Improvement teams. Barbara began her career within the M&A division of Banca Leonardo (now Houlihan Lokey) in Milan.
Barbara holds a MSc in Finance and a BSc in Economics and Social Sciences from Bocconi University and an MBA from INSEAD. She speaks Italian and English.
Daniel Knight
Senior Investment Director
Daniel joined Three Hills in November 2023 and is a Senior Investment Director. Daniel previously spent over six years at Bridges Fund Management in London investing in high growth, impactful businesses across the UK and Europe, and also represented Bridges as a Board Director of multiple portfolio companies. Prior to Bridges, he spent a year at special situations investor Agathos and five years in the Deals practice at PwC.
Daniel completed the ACA while at PwC, holds an MSc in Economics from University College London and a BSc in Economics from Cardiff University
Fred Kinsman
Investment Director
Based in the London House, Fred Kinsman joined Three Hills as an Investment Director in September 2025.
Fred previously spent four years in Direct Lending at Investec Bank (London) originating and executing credit investments in lower middle market companies across UK, Benelux and DACH. Prior to Investec, he spent six years in leverage finance and private debt at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia (Sydney) executing leveraged buy-outs and growth financing across the Australasian market.
Monica Perricone
Investment Director
Monica Perricone joined Three Hills in February 2019 and is a Senior Investment Manager. Before joining the company, Monica spent 4 years at Deutsche Bank in the European Leveraged Finance Group and Equity Capital Markets.
Monica holds an MSc in Finance cum laude from Bocconi University. She speaks Italian and English.
Bilal Tahir
Investment Director
Bilal joined Three Hills in February 2022 and is a Senior Investment Manager

AA
The AA is the largest roadside assistance provider by market share in the UK, servicing a large portion of the consumer and manufacturer segments, as well as the UK’s largest fleet and leasing companies. With more than 115 years of operating history, the AA is one of the most widely recognized and trusted brands in the UK and has effectively built upon this brand to become an established provider of insurance broking, insurance underwriting and driving services.
visit website
Acacium Group
Acacium Group provides specialized staffing, workforce management solutions and managed services to the healthcare, social care and life sciences sectors internationally. Active across four continents, the company plays a vital role in private and public healthcare systems, providing solutions to address the structural imbalances between workforce supply and demand, and delivering preventative care and community services that support hospitals and other healthcare providers, as well as the clinical activities of life sciences companies.
visit website
Access Financial
Access utilizes proprietary analytics and a flexible technology platform to provide various credit and related financial services and products to the financially underserved consumer credit market. Access applies the experiences gained and infrastructure built from servicing over $25 billion in consumer loans over its 23-year operating history, to support lenders who originate a range of consumer loan products. These products include retail credit and credit cards marketed through multiple channels, including retail point of sale, direct mail solicitation and partnerships with third parties.
ACPS Automotive
ACPS Automotive is a manufacturer of tow bars for original equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket. The company is headquartered near Stuttgart in Germany and has manufacturing facilities in Germany, Hungary and Mexico. It is an innovator in the tow bar market, inventing the retractable tow bar in the early 2000s and introducing the first fully electric retractable tow bar in 2010.
visit website
Aernnova
Aernnova is a fully integrated end-to-end Tier 1 aircraft aerostructures manufacturer and engineer. The company has manufacturing facilities in Spain, Portugal, U.K., the U.S., Brazil and Mexico and provides composite and metallic components and engineering services to major original equipment manufacturers such as Airbus, Embraer and Boeing.
visit website
AIM Aviation
During the period of TowerBrook Fund III’s investment, AIM Aviation designed, engineered and manufactured cabin interiors for the world’s major airlines and original equipment manufacturers including Airbus and Boeing. Its offering included stowages and galleys, premium monuments and bar units, lounges, sky shops and seat modules. TowerBrook exited its investment in 2016 via the sale of AIM Aviation to AVIC International Aero-Development Corporation, a Chinese multinational aviation company.
Amylu Foods
Amylu is a manufacturer of value-added chicken products, including sausages, meatballs and burgers, sold under the Amylu brand and private label. The company’s broad portfolio of innovative and flavorful products is tailored to address consumer preferences for all-natural, high-protein options with verifiable health attributes (e.g., organic, antibiotic-free, nitrate-free) paired with unmatched convenience.
visit website
ApplePie SPV
ApplePie SPV was a vehicle formed in 2016 by TowerBrook’s TSO Fund I in partnership with ApplePie Capital to make investments in the specialty franchise lending space. The vehicle provided funding that enabled ApplePie to originate franchise finance loans to prime borrowers operating select brands. ApplePie SPV disposed of substantially all of its loan portfolio in 2018.
AQUAchiara
AQUAchiara is a European provider of microfiltered water dispenser solutions for hotels, restaurants and corporate clients. Its mission is to refine locally sourced tap water into fresh, sparkling, high-quality water through advanced microfiltration technology. Committed to environmental sustainability, AQUAchiara aims to offer an eco-friendly alternative, reducing reliance on bottled water and avoiding considerable CO
2
emissions from production and transportation.
visit website
Archimica
During the period of TowerBrook Fund II’s investment, Archimica was a manufacturer of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and late-stage intermediates for the pharmaceutical industry. An API is the active molecule in a drug and is the component of the final pharmaceutical product that gives it its remedial properties.
visit website
AustroCel Hallein
AustroCel Hallein operates one of Europe’s major integrated biorefineries, transforming sustainably sourced forestry byproducts into high-value biofuels, bioperformance and biomaterials products. Based in Austria, the company operates a zero-waste, circular model utilizing 100% of its raw materials.
visit website
Auto Europe
During the period of TowerBrook Fund I’s investment, Auto Europe was a global distributor of leisure car rental services. The company operated three primary business units: Auto Europe (North America), brokering car rentals for outbound North American travelers to Europe; Auto Europe (Europe), brokering car rentals for intra-Europe travelers; and DriveAway Holidays, brokering car rentals for outbound Australian travellers to Europe.
visit website
Autodistribution Group
During the period of TowerBrook Fund III’s investment, Autodistribution Group was a vertically integrated distributor of automotive parts in the French and European aftermarket, with an extensive network of suppliers supporting professional firms, mainly garages, repair shops, fleet managers and industrial customers. TowerBrook exited its investment in 2015 via the sale of Autodistribution Group to Bain Capital.
visit website
Axil
Axil is a waste consultancy and solution service disruptor primarily focused on large manufacturing and industrial sites with complex waste streams. Axil’s consultative, total resource management solution specializes in innovative waste reduction, segregation, recycling, and resource recovery across the UK, thereby reducing emissions, pollution, and ecosystem damage from waste disposal.
visit website
Azzurri Group
Azzurri Group is a multi-cuisine hospitality platform operating Zizzi and ASK Italian (two national Italian full-service brands), Coco di Mama (a quick-service Italian food-to-go concept), Boojum (fast-casual Mexican chain) and recently the fried chicken QSR brand Dave’s Hot Chicken. Azzurri also owns Openr, an innovative tech start-up providing a product, pricing and order management technology platform.
visit website
Battea
During the period of TowerBrook’s TSO II investment, Battea Class Action Services was a provider of securities claims management services to nearly 1,000 global financial institutions, including many of the world’s largest banks, hedge funds, asset managers and buy-side investors. TowerBrook exited its investment in 2024 via a sale to a wholly owned subsidiary of SS&C Technology Holdings Inc.
visit website
BevMo!
During the period of TowerBrook Fund II’s investment, BevMo! was a large specialty retailer of alcoholic drinks and related items in the U.S. The company had over 150 stores located throughout California, Arizona and Washington. The typical 10,000-square-foot store carried a large assortment of products including over 3,800 wines, 2,400 spirits and 2,400 beers, together with a wide variety of complementary products ranging from cocktail napkins and snack items to glassware and bar accessories.
visit website
Braas Monier
During the period of TowerBrook Fund III’s investment, Braas Monier (then Monier Group), formerly the roofing division of Lafarge Group, was a global roofing company with over 80 operational business units in 35 countries. The business provided intelligent roofing solutions, chimney, energy and ventilation systems, roof tiles and roofing components. In 2014, Braas Monier completed an IPO on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. TowerBrook exited its investment in Braas Monier in 2016.
BRG
BRG is a global consulting firm specializing in disputes and investigations, corporate finance, and performance improvement. Headquartered in Emeryville, California, BRG has over 1,600 professionals in more than 40 offices across the U.S., Asia, Australia, Canada, Latin America, the Middle East and the U.K..
visit website
Bruneau
Founded in 1955, Bruneau is one of the largest European online B2B distributors of office equipment products. The company primarily addresses small and mid-size enterprises and offers over 100,000 different items, with 6,000 orders processed every day and 7.3 million packages dispatched per annum.
visit website
Cablecom GmbH
During the period of TowerBrook Fund I’s investment, Cablecom GmbH was the largest cable communications provider in Switzerland, providing a wide range of services including cable television, Internet access and telephony services to consumer and business customers. The company served approximately two million analogue cable television subscribers, through its own network and partner networks, representing approximately 73% of the Swiss cable television market at the time.

Championing Talent
TowerBrook is committed to supporting a talented workforce that embodies integrity, teamwork and respect for others and encourages new ideas and perspectives.
We believe that talented teams with diverse ways of thinking make better decisions, and better decisions lead to better businesses. TowerBrook’s support for diversity and equal opportunity is integral to our culture and at the core of our identity as a firm. Our commitment to equality of opportunity is reflected in our Responsible Ownership Statement and our Purpose Statement.
Our Operating Committee, comprised of senior professionals from across the firm, leads the development and assessment of our initiatives related to attracting and supporting talent. We seek to recruit exceptional talent from a broad pool of candidates and ensure that we are supporting, mentoring, developing and retaining highly talented people over the long term. We seek to build effective and high-performing Boards and management teams with diverse viewpoints and competencies in the companies we control. We have implemented anti-harassment, equal opportunity employment, equitable remuneration, and whistleblowing and complaints policies and procedures, and we encourage our portfolio companies to do the same.
As a firm, we are also committed to fostering a work environment and career progression path that is supportive to primary and secondary caregivers, as reflected in our parental leave policy.
We continue to develop metrics to help us track the progress of our firm and our portfolio companies in promoting a diverse and inclusive working environment. We keep our policies and initiatives, and our evaluation of their effectiveness, under constant review.
Click
here
to view our Championing Talent Report 2025.
Equal Employment Opportunity Policy
TowerBrook is an equal employment opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.
TowerBrook’s Affinity Groups are voluntary, employee-driven resource groups that are organized around a particular shared interest, characteristic or experience. Groups are open to all team members, including allies.
TowerBrook’s Affinity Groups work to:
Promote diversity, cultural awareness, and an inclusive work environment
Foster professional development and learning throughout the firm through mentoring, networking, open dialogue and the exchange of ideas
Provide support and resources for employees
Help the firm attract, recruit, and retain talented employees with a broad range of perspectives
Reinforce TowerBrook’s talent and health and wellness initiatives internally and in our wider industry

Our firm supports

We support Level 20’s five key initiatives to achieve this mission: mentoring and development; networking and events; outreach; advocacy; and research. We encourage our employees, irrespective of gender, to be active members of Level 20 by contributing to Level 20-led research, discussion groups and outreach events and participating in the annual mentoring program.

Our Investments
Trilantic Europe focuses on sectors where we have significant resources, experience and expertise and can capitalise on our diversified sourcing and operating relationships and capabilities. Our sectors of focus are Consumer & Leisure, Industrials, TMT, Business Services and Healthcare.
Sectors
Portfolio
Advisers with sector expertise
Consumer & Leisure
Advisers with sector expertise
The Consumer & Leisure sector is a longstanding area of focus for Trilantic Europe. Investments in the sector have been made by each of our last three Funds, dating back to 2003. Utilising the broad expertise of our team and of our operating Partners, we focus particularly on Food and Food Ingredients, Beauty Products, Luxury and Leisure & Entertainment.
Our portfolio companies typically have strong brands and market positioning, while those in the leisure segment enjoy positive market dynamics driven by demographics and consumption/experience trends.
Companies in this sector include:
Advisers with sector expertise
Industrials & Energy Transition
Advisers with sector expertise
Trilantic Europe has a long history of investing in Industrial & Energy Transition related companies often backing family or founder owned businesses as they undergo intergenerational transitions, international expansion or spin-off from larger industrial conglomerates. With a strong base of Industrial, Manufacturing and Engineering companies in Europe, Trilantic Europe has in particular focused on transportation, automotive and e-mobility and, increasingly over the last years, successfully focused on energy transition to support the secular trend in carbon footprint and emissions reduction.
Companies in this sector include:
Advisers with sector expertise
TMT
Advisers with sector expertise
Historically, Trilantic Europe has closely monitored the Telecom sector in Europe and been able to support companies at times where hands-on value-added capital was required to support investments, growth or operational improvements. Our commitment to Telecom and Media has recently been complemented by increased focus on Technology, Software and Internet related businesses.
Companies in this sector include:
Advisers with sector expertise
Business Services
Advisers with sector expertise
Trilantic Europe typically focuses on asset light companies with high cash conversion rates, and significant potential for international expansion that we can support. Buy and Build has been a particularly relevant strategy for this sector.
Companies in this sector include:
Advisers with sector expertise
Healthcare
Advisers with sector expertise
Healthcare expenditure represents between 9% and 11% of GDP in all European countries. With positive macro trends in Europe, including ageing populations, increased life expectancy and growing government deficits in some countries, Trilantic Europe continues to actively search for opportunities in the sector.
Our deep-rooted presence in each of the geographies we target, together with our strong industry expertise supported by 3 operating partners, means we are well positioned to invest in the complex European healthcare landscape. Differing payment, regulatory and social factors create unique characteristics in each country and provide an opportunity for us to employ our specialist knowledge and expertise. Trilantic Europe has been particularly active in Medical Services and Facilities, but also in Pharma Ingredients and Contract Manufacturing where we believe there are good consolidation opportunities for companies that can offer efficient manufacturing and operational standards.
Companies in this sector include:
In addition, Trilantic Europe focuses on specific Technology verticals where it can leverage its industry and country presence and preserve its focus on cash flow generating businesses. Sector verticals include: network infrastructure, software, IT services and tech enabled businesses.

About
About
Unlocking potential – whatever the weather
Triton was founded in 1997 and is owned by its active partners. We are an operationally minded investment firm that aims to generate strong returns regardless of economic conditions.
We do this by investing in what we believe are future winners. These companies operate in growing markets, are backed by favourable long-term trends, and have untapped potential. We focus on sectors we know well and have a strong track record in: Industrial Tech, Business Services, and Healthcare.
Our approach is to
Buy Well
,
Build Better Businesses
, and
Sell Growth
. We aim to be smart in finding investment opportunities, help unlock potential and transform them into higher-quality companies that are built to last.
Triton benefits from the support of Accelerator Unit, a dedicated management services provider. Accelerator Unit, comprising more than 50 experts, specialises in helping companies achieve sustainable, strategic, operational, and financial improvements.

Who we are - 21 Invest
Who we are
We are an established investment firm, with an experienced team of professionals.
We leverage our entrepreneurial mindset to help portfolio companies in their growth.
About us
For the last 30 years, we have provided companies with the tools and expertise they need to help them reach their full potential and pursue long term expansion.
We trace our roots back to the enlightened vision of Alessandro Benetton, embodying a commitment to social consciousness, innovation, and continuous improvement that permeates every aspect of our work.
Founded in 1992, 21 Invest was a pioneer in the Italian mid-market. We continued evolving with the establishment of a local team in France in 1998. More recently, we further expanded our geographic focus into Spain and the Benelux.
Today we are a European group, with a strong local presence to scout investment opportunities and support portfolio companies growth, along with a global coordination on industry knowledge, investor relations, sustainability and communications.
Our pillars
What makes us stand out.
1. History and heritage
Born almost 30 years ago, today we are recognized for our strong heritage, values and reputation.
2. Experience and flexibility
We are a team of about 50 professionals with a mindset built around high quality technical and soft skills.
3. Active Ownership
We work alongside companies providing support and guidance to make them reach their growth and efficiency objectives.
4. Sustainability practice
We believe in environmental, social and business sustainability and are the first investment company to have partnered with the Shared Value initiative.

Insights – 2/18/2026
Video: Missy Dolski on Värde’s Approach to Asset-Based Finance
Asset‑based finance is a growing asset class that offers investors diversifying private credit exposure backed by tangible collateral. Värde’s strategy focuses on middle‑market opportunities across commercial and consumer asset classes, as well as fund finance. We are a true solutions provider that acquires assets, finances assets, and lends directly to origination platforms and funds that otherwise originate these loans. Our transactions span across trade finance and equipment leasing to credit cards and student loans. We draw on asset expertise, long-standing relationships, and a dedicated data‑science team to support differentiated sourcing, strong execution and resilient, cash‑flowing exposure for investors.

The Italian Leader in Early-Stage investments
Pioneering investments, focusing on talent
Zest Investments continuously scouts for visionary entrepreneurs that are looking for a partner that can work with them and help them grow. The unique Zest ecosystem of investors, Founders and Corporates, combined with over 20 years of experience and expertise grants our portfolio with the needed support to become market leaders.
Zest Investments is always on the lookout for the next trends that are shaping the market and investing at an early stage that allows us to have the pulse on what is happening in the ecosystem around us.
Our secret sauce is made of our own entrepreneurial background together with an industrial approach and full package of services, make us the partner your startup needs to be the next big thing.

Le persone
Le persone sono al centro
del percorso di sviluppo e consolidamento del Gruppo Yarpa:
“Il Gruppo è impegnato nel promuovere la parità di genere, età, etnia, orientamento sessuale, identità o espressione di genere, condizione personale, provenienza geografica e credo religioso, garantendo un’uguaglianza di trattamento, anche in termini di parità salariale in relazione alle mansioni svolte, alle responsabilità attribuite, alla seniority e al merito, e pari opportunità di carriera a tutti i dipendenti, ad ogni livello aziendale.”
Yarpa promuove altresì la continua formazione delle proprie persone
, volta alla valorizzazione delle potenzialità di ogni individuo, ricercando la più alta qualità nello svolgimento delle diverse mansioni.

il Gruppo conta circa 30 professionisti
